beats.text: Most fights get worse the longer they go. Here's how to stop that!
Three tips from decades of couples research. Save this!
Tip one: start soft! In one study, the first three minutes of a fight predicted whether newlyweds divorced years later.
Tip two: keep it five to one. Stable couples have about five positive moments for every negative one. Even while fighting! And tip three?
Take a break! When your heart races, you stop listening. Gottman recommends at least twenty minutes.
So: start soft. Stay kind. And pause!

ask: SAVE THIS FOR YOUR NEXT FIGHT.
sources: Carrère & Gottman (1999), Predicting divorce among newlyweds from the first three minutes of a marital conflict discussion, Family Process 38(3).
Gottman & Levenson – observational conflict studies; stable couples ~5:1 positive-to-negative interactions during conflict (Gottman Institute, 'The Magic Relationship Ratio').
Gottman – physiological 'flooding'; recommended break of at least 20 minutes (Gottman Institute; The Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work, 1999).
